lesson: The domain prior was useful: corruption investigations tied to contracts, licensing and export revenue made the Oil Ministry the strongest single ministry. Preserve this kind of sector-to-institution mapping, while retaining meaningful alternatives when no named official or case file is available.

A 99.7 percent single-name forecast was indefensible for a discretionary acting appointment. For Trump personnel succession, enumerate statutory successors and prominent cross-agency loyalists, including unconventional choices such as Bill Pulte, and never infer near certainty from one reported front-runner without an official designation.

The forecast omitted the eventual primary winner entirely. For state primaries, build the candidate set from the certified ballot and recent local reporting before assigning national-name priors; low-profile insurgents and late momentum must retain explicit probability.

A rescheduled private political dinner need not remain at the event's traditional venue. Venue forecasts should include hotels with sufficient capacity and strong organizer or administration ties; the Waldorf Astoria was a realistic Washington alternative that should not have been omitted.

Generic former-minister priors were a poor substitute for tracing the UN regional rotation, endorsed national candidate and formal nomination record. For multilateral leadership elections, identify the relevant regional slate before forecasting recognizable international figures.

Keeping both leading former presidents and giving Sharif Sheikh Ahmed a narrow lead was appropriately calibrated. Continue using current residence, protest alignment and local coalition signals rather than collapsing a close Somali opposition question to one name.

Bahrain's exposure as host of the US Fifth Fleet deserved much more weight than cumulative regional strike counts suggested. Pair-valued outcomes are also order-sensitive in the scoring data: use the most likely source ordering, because 'Bahrain and Kuwait' did not match the recorded 'Kuwait and Bahrain' even though it named the same countries.
